taken by UMA for the skim/gouge-law decision @ 9cea9fe

Skim/gouge-law decision (UMA) @ f3e11d1

**Verdict: (b). Main's wire law judged every move with the rough pass's kerf; the skim offsets are right.**

The test's conditions (wire Ø0.25, so r = 0.125; punch, part's left side at X-20):
- rough C110: gap 0.04, offset 0.165 (X-20.165)
- skim 1 S21: gap 0.02, offset 0.145 (X-20.145)
- skim 2 S31: gap 0.01, offset 0.135 (X-20.135)

The rough pass is moves 1-7, so move 8 is skim 1's lead-in to X-20.145 Y0. Main's `wire_verify` handed the law one half-width, 0.125 + 0.04 = 0.165, for every move. Measured that way, move 8 enters by 0.165 - 0.145 = **0.0200 mm**, exactly the reported finding. Each pass really burns only its own r + g, so every pass's kerf edge, the last skim's included, sits on the outline (0.145 - 0.145 = 0 and 0.135 - 0.135 = 0). The last skim sets the finished size, and the 0.03 mm between the rough and the last skim is the stock the skims remove.

**Fix (b), with the law kept conservative.** `WireJob.skim_offsets` carries each skim's own r + g, read from the same condition table the generator uses. The new `sim/src/verify/wire/passes.rs` splits the path at each return to the threading point (the rule `announce_skims` already uses) and judges each move at its own pass's half-width. That half-width is the real kerf of that pass, never narrower. The threading law takes the widest pass's kerf, and the slug law sweeps each pass at its own offset and joins the results. If the path does not return once per stated pass, or an open run states skims, the law refuses it by name. Skims on an open run are also refused at the door (`check_passes`). The arithmetic is in `docs/decisions/538-wire-skims.md`.

Pinned by `sim verify::wire::tests::each_pass_is_judged_at_its_own_kerf`. That test shows the path is clean at its own kerf, that the single-offset reading reproduces the false gouge at move 8 with depth K - ks, and that a skim 0.05 mm too near is still a 0.05 mm gouge at move 8. Also pinned by `passes_that_cannot_be_told_apart_are_unreadable`, motion `skim_laws_refuse_by_name` (open run), and `wire_post::a_rough_and_two_skims_post_three_offsets_and_condition_selects`, which now posts through the gate. Golden `wire_contour_punch_skims.nc` is **unchanged** (byte-identical).

**Per-file resolutions (both sides kept):**
- `operation/types/mod.rs`, `types/wire_edm.rs`: main's 4-axis/tabs types and exports plus `WireSkim`/`SKIMS_MAX`. `is_sane` keeps `sane_id` + the skim bounds + main's tabs check.
- `operation/wire_op.rs`: `WireCondition` carries both `skims` and main's `machine`/`max_taper_deg`. `condition_of` keeps the per-skim lookup and `check_passes`, and adds main's burnout clearance door. The cut-off probe clears the skims (it reads the cut-off condition alone). Generation is main's taper/burnout/tabs/4-axis path exactly when there are no skims, and `wire_passes` otherwise. New `skims_refusal`: skims beside a taper, burnout, tabs or 4-axis cut are refused by name at the door (inside `condition_of`) and at generation.
- `motion/wire_edm/mod.rs`: both module lists. `cut_pass` keeps main's tabbed walk and the start-point push, plus the PR's reverse; a reversed tabbed pass is refused by name. `notes` keeps main's signature; the reversed note is `pass_notes`. `skims.rs` `check_passes` refuses tabs beside skims.
- `sim/verify/wire/{mod,slug,passes}.rs`: main's leaning `Wire` stays the one reading of the path. `Pass` is now an index range on it. `passes::gouge_at` is `kerf::gouge_at` per pass at its own kerf, with the lean's widening kept. The slug law sweeps each pass's section at each height at its own offset and joins them. With no skims both are main's law exactly. The open-run skims refusal is kept, and a tabbed cut stating skims is read as unreadable.
- `posting_wire.rs`: main's `section`/`guided` split. `announce_skims` runs on the untabbed section; a tabbed path stating skims is refused.
- `project/wire_edm_dto.rs`: both fields and DTOs.
- Tests: `wire_post.rs`, `wire_readers.rs`, `wire_verify.rs`, `posted_gates/wire.rs`, the motion/sim test files, the ui `wire_page.rs` destructure (main's). Literal-only additions of `skims`/`skim_offsets` in `wire_{4axis,burnout,stamp,tabs,taper}.rs`, `posted_gates/wire_4axis.rs`, sim `hold_tests.rs`/`taper_tests.rs`. Pinning tests ok: `verify::wire::tests::each_pass_is_judged_at_its_own_kerf`, `passes_that_cannot_be_told_apart_are_unreadable`, `wire_edm::tests::skim_laws_refuse_by_name`, `a_rough_and_two_skims_post_three_offsets_and_condition_selects`. The gate's clippy step was red on one `collapsible_if` in my resolution (`wire_op.rs`, behaviour-neutral). After the fix, `cargo clippy -p geometry,cl,tools,post,sim,motion,app,ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The suites were not re-run after that one-line fix.

**Blocker - main moved during the gate (#1506 Sodick wire post, #1528, #1518):**
1. `crates/app/tests/sodick_wire_post.rs` (new in main) builds a `WireContourOp` without `skims`, so this head merged into today's main does not compile. The fix is a one-line test literal.
2. **Unsafe:** `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps` writes its C condition word once, at section start (`block([condition])`). A later `PARAM EdmCondition` only reassigns the variable. A skimmed Wire Contour posted through the Sodick post would cut every skim with the rough pass's C word, and nothing would refuse it: wrong G-code. Before this PR can merge, the Sodick post must either refuse a mid-section condition change by name or write the new C word at each pass. That is post logic (safety floor), not a merge resolution, so I stopped here.

Hand-resolved refresh (DELTA) - needs a second refresh for #1506 plus a Sodick-post decision before it is ready for a re-check (M3/M5).
